devanagari: रोचते यदि वा सख्यं बाहुरेष प्रसारितः ।
translit: rocate yadi vā sakhyaṃ bāhureṣa prasāritaḥ, gṛhyatāṃ pāṇinā pāṇirmaryādā vadhyatāṃ dhruvā
en: If indeed this friendship (sakhya) is agreeable, then this arm of mine is extended (towards you). Let hand be grasped by hand, and a firm, lasting bond be established.
Having heard these well-spoken words of Sugrīva, Rāma, with a thoroughly joyful mind, grasped his hand with his own. Sustaining their heartfelt friendship (sauhṛda), he embraced him closely.

translit: tato hanūmān saṃtyajya bhikṣurūpamariṃdamaḥ, kāṣṭhayoḥ svena rūpeṇa janayāmāsa pāvakam
en: Then, Hanuman, the subduer of foes, abandoning his mendicant disguise, produced fire from two pieces of wood in his true form.

translit: dīpyamānaṃ tato vahniṃ puṣpairabhyarcya satkṛtam, tayormadhye tu suprīto nidadhe susamāhitaḥ
en: Then, after worshipping the blazing, honored fire with flowers, Hanuman, being very pleased and perfectly composed, placed it between the two (Rama and Sugriva).

devanagari: ततो ऽग्निं दीप्यमानं तौ चक्रतुश्च प्रदक्षिणम् ।
translit: tato'gniṃ dīpyamānaṃ tau cakratuśca pradakṣiṇam, sugrīvo rāghavaścaiva vayasyatvamupāgatau
en: Then, the two of them (Rama and Sugriva) circumambulated the blazing fire. And thus, Sugriva and Rama certainly attained friendship.

devanagari: मायावी नाम तेजस्वी पूर्वजो दुन्दुभेः सुतः ।
तेन तस्य महद्वैरं स्त्रीकृतं विश्रुतं पुरा ॥
translit: māyāvī nāma tejasvī pūrvajo dundubheḥ sutaḥ, tena tasya mahadvairaṃ strīkṛtaṃ viśrutaṃ purā
en: Māyāvī, a powerful figure and the elder son of Dundubhi, had, in former times, a great and widely known enmity with Vālī, which originated from a woman.

devanagari: स तृणैरावृतं दुर्गं धरण्या विवरं महत् ।
translit: sa tṛṇairāvṛtaṃ durgaṃ dharaṇyā vivaraṃ mahat, praviveśāsuro vegādāvāmāsādya viṣṭhitau
en: He, the demon, swiftly entered a large, grass-covered, inaccessible cavern in the earth, just as we two approached and stood (at its entrance).

devanagari: तं प्रविष्टं रिपुं दृष्ट्वा बिलं रोषवशं गतः ।
translit: taṃ praviṣṭaṃ ripuṃ dṛṣṭvā bilaṃ roṣavaśaṃ gataḥ, māmuvāca tadā vālī vacanaṃ kṣubhitendriyaḥ
en: Seeing that enemy enter the hole, Vali became overcome with rage, his senses greatly agitated, and then he spoke these words to me.

devanagari: इह त्वं तिष्ठ सुग्रीव बिलद्वारि समाहितः ।
translit: iha tvaṃ tiṣṭha sugrīva biladvāri samāhitaḥ, yāvadatra praviśyāhaṃ nihanmi samare ripum
en: Sugriva, you remain here at the cave entrance, attentive. As long as I enter and kill the enemy in battle.

devanagari: मया त्वेतद्वचः श्रुत्वा याचितः स परंतप ।
शापयित्वा च मां पद्भ्यां प्रविवेश बिलं तदा ॥
translit: mayā tvetadvacaḥ śrutvā yācitaḥ sa paraṃtapa, śāpayitvā ca māṃ padbhyāṃ praviveśa bilaṃ tadā
en: But after I (Sugriva) heard these words (from Vali), he (Vali), O tormentor of foes, was implored by me. He then made me swear by his feet and entered the cave.

devanagari: तस्य प्रविष्टस्य बिलं साग्रः संवत्सरो गतः ।
स्थितस्य च मम द्वारि स कालो व्यत्यवर्तत ॥
translit: tasya praviṣṭasya bilaṃ sāgraḥ saṃvatsaro gataḥ, sthitasya ca mama dvāri sa kālo vyatyavartata
en: A full year passed after he (Vali) entered the cave. And that much time elapsed while I remained at the entrance.

translit: atha dīrghasya kālasya bilāttasmādviniḥsṛtam, saphenaṃ rudhiraṃ raktamahaṃ dṛṣṭvā suduḥkhitaḥ
en: Then, after a long time, frothy, red blood emerged from that cave. Having seen it, I became greatly distressed.

devanagari: निरस्तस्य च संग्रामे क्रोशतो निःस्वनो गुरोः ॥
translit: nardatāmasurāṇāṃ ca dhvanirme śrotramāgataḥ, nirastasya ca saṃgrāme krośato niḥsvano guroḥ
en: And the roar of the bellowing demons came to my ear, and (also) the crying sound of my elder brother (guru), who was defeated in battle.

But, my friend, by those signs, I understood intellectually that my brother was killed. And, having covered the cave entrance with a mountain-sized rock, and overwhelmed with sorrow, I performed the water oblation and came to Kishkindha.

devanagari: गूहमानस्य मे तत्त्वं यत्नतो मन्त्रिभिः श्रुतम् ।
translit: gūhamānasya me tattvaṃ yatnato mantribhiḥ śrutam, tato'haṃ taiḥ samāgamya sametairabhiṣecitaḥ
en: While I was trying to conceal it, the truth was carefully heard by the ministers. Thereafter, having met with those assembled ministers, I was consecrated (as king).

translit: rājyaṃ praśāsatastasya nyāyato mama rāghava, ājagāma ripuṃ hatvā vālī tamasurottamam
en: O Rāghava, while I was justly ruling his kingdom, Vāli returned, having slain that formidable enemy, the best of asuras.

devanagari: अभिषिक्तं तु मां दृष्ट्वा क्रोधात् संरक्तलोचनः ।
translit: abhiṣiktaṃ tu māṃ dṛṣṭvā krodhāt saṃraktalocanaḥ, madīyānmantriṇo baddhvā paruṣaṃ vākyamabravīt
en: But when he saw me, already consecrated, his eyes became bloodshot with rage, and having imprisoned my ministers, he uttered harsh words.

devanagari: स्निग्धमेवं ब्रुवाणं मां स तु निर्भर्त्स्य वानरः ।
धिक् त्वामिति च मामुक्त्वा बहु तत्तदुवाच ह ॥
translit: snigdhamevaṃ bruvāṇaṃ māṃ sa tu nirbhartsya vānaraḥ, dhik tvāmiti ca māmuktvā bahu tattaduvāca ha
en: But that monkey, having harshly rebuked me who was speaking thus affectionately, and having told me 'Shame on you!', indeed said many other things.

devanagari: अहत्वा नास्ति मे शक्तिः प्रतिगन्तुमितः पुरीम् ।
translit: ahatvā nāsti me śaktiḥ pratigantumitaḥ purīm, biladvāri pratīkṣa tvaṃ yāvadenaṃ nihanmyaham
en: Without killing him, I have no strength (śakti) to return to the city from here. You wait at the cave's entrance until I kill him.

devanagari: स्थितो ऽयमिति मत्वा तु प्रविष्टो ऽहं दुरासदम् ।
तं च मे मार्गमाणस्य गतः संवत्सरस्तदा ॥
translit: sthito'yamiti matvā tu praviṣṭo'haṃ durāsadam, taṃ ca me mārgamāṇasya gataḥ saṃvatsarastadā
en: Having thought, 'He is staying here,' I entered that difficult-to-access place. And while I was searching for him, a year (saṃvatsara) passed by then.

devanagari: निहतश्च मया तत्र सो ऽसुरो बन्धुभिः सह ॥
translit: sa tu dṛṣṭo mayā śatruranirvedādbhayāvahaḥ, nihataśca mayā tatra so'suro bandhubhiḥ saha
en: But that fearsome enemy (śatru) was found by me through perseverance, and that demon (asura), along with his kinsmen, was killed by me there.

devanagari: सूदयित्वा तु तं शत्रुं विक्रान्तं दुन्दुभेः सुतम् ।
translit: sūdayitvā tu taṃ śatruṃ vikrāntaṃ dundubheḥ sutam, niṣkrāmanneva paśyāmi bilasya pihitaṃ mukham
en: After I had killed that mighty enemy, the son of Dundubhi, as I was just exiting, I saw that the cave entrance was closed.

devanagari: विक्रोशमानस्य तु मे सुग्रीवेति पुनः पुनः ।
यदा प्रतिवचो नास्ति ततो ऽहं भृशदुःखितः ॥
translit: vikrośamānasya tu me sugrīveti punaḥ punaḥ, yadā prativaco nāsti tato'haṃ bhṛśaduḥkhitaḥ
en: But when there was no reply to me, even as I was shouting 'Sugrīva!' repeatedly, then I became exceedingly distressed.

devanagari: ततो ऽहं तेन निष्क्रम्य यथा पुनरुपागतः ॥
translit: pādaprahāraistu mayā bahuśastadvidāritam, tato'haṃ tena niṣkramya yathā punarupāgataḥ
en: But I repeatedly broke open that [cave entrance] with kicks. Then, having exited through that opening, I returned as I had come.

translit: tatrānenāsmi saṃruddho rājyaṃ mārgayatātmanaḥ, sugrīveṇa nṛśaṃsena vismṛtya bhrātṛsauhṛdam
en: In that situation, I was obstructed by this cruel Sugrīva, who was seeking the kingdom for himself, having forgotten brotherly affection.

devanagari: एवमुक्त्वा तु मां तत्र वस्त्रेणैकेन वानरः ।
translit: evamuktvā tu māṃ tatra vastreṇaikena vānaraḥ, tadā nirvāsayāmāsa vālī vigatasādhvasaḥ
en: Thus having spoken to me there, Valin, that fearless monkey, then expelled me with only one garment.

translit: tenāhamapaviddhaśca hṛtadāraśca rāghava, tadbhayācca mahīkṛtsnā krānteyaṃ savanārṇavā
en: O Raghava, by him I was cast out and my wife was seized. And due to fear of him, this entire earth, with its forests and oceans, has been traversed.

translit: ṛśyamūkaṃ girivaraṃ bhāryāharaṇaduḥkhitaḥ, praviṣṭo'smi durādharṣaṃ vālinaḥ kāraṇāntare
en: Grieving from the abduction of my wife, I entered Rishyamuka, the foremost of mountains, which is inaccessible to Valin due to a specific reason.

translit: tamevamuktvā saṃkruddho mālāmutkṣipya kāñcanīm, pitrā dattāṃ mahendreṇa yuddhāya vyavatiṣṭhata
en: Having spoken thus to him, greatly enraged, [Vali] threw up the golden garland which had been given to him by his father, Mahendra (Indra), and stood ready for battle.

devanagari: स गृहीत्वा धनुर्घोरं शरमेकं च मानदः ।
translit: sa gṛhītvā dhanurghoraṃ śaramekaṃ ca mānadaḥ, sālānuddiśya cikṣepa jyāsvanaiḥ pūrayandiśaḥ
en: He, the bestower of honor, having grasped the mighty bow and a single arrow, aimed at the śāla trees and shot, filling all directions with the resonant twangs of his bowstring.

devanagari: भित्त्वा सालान् गिरिप्रस्थे सप्त भूमिं विवेश ह ॥
translit: sa visṛṣṭo balavatā bāṇaḥ svarṇapariṣkṛtaḥ, bhittvā sālān giriprasthe sapta bhūmiṃ viveśa ha
en: That gold-adorned arrow, discharged by the powerful Rāma, having pierced the seven śāla trees on the mountain plateau, indeed entered the earth.

devanagari: निष्पत्य च पुनस्तूर्णं स्वतूणीं प्रविवेश ह ॥
translit: praviṣṭastu muhūrtena rasāṃ bhittvā mahājavaḥ, niṣpatya ca punastūrṇaṃ svatūṇīṃ praviveśa ha
en: That arrow, possessing immense speed, pierced the earth (rasā) in an instant, and having emerged, swiftly re-entered its own quiver.

translit: asmādgacchāma kiṣkindhāṃ kṣipraṃ gaccha tvamagrataḥ, gatvā cāhvaya sugrīva vālinaṃ bhrātṛgandhinam
en: From here, let us proceed to Kiṣkindhā. You (Sugrīva), go quickly ahead. And once there, Sugrīva, summon Vālin, who is a brother merely in name.

devanagari: सर्वे ते त्वरितं गत्वा किष्किन्धां वालिनः पुरीम् ।
translit: sarve te tvaritaṃ gatvā kiṣkindhāṃ vālinaḥ purīm, vṛkṣairātmānamāvṛtya vyatiṣṭhan gahane vane
en: All of them, having quickly reached Kiṣkindhā, the city of Vālin, concealed themselves among the trees and remained in the dense forest.

translit: sugrīvo vyanadadghoraṃ vālino hvānakāraṇāt, gāḍhaṃ parihito vegānnādairbhindannivāmbaram
en: Sugrīva let out a terrible roar, intending to challenge Vālin. Firmly prepared, he burst forth with impetuous energy, with roars as if tearing the very sky.

devanagari: ततो रामो धनुष्पाणिस्ताव् उभौ समुदीक्ष्य तु ।
translit: tato rāmo dhanuṣpāṇistāv ubhau samudīkṣya tu, anyonyasadṛśau vīrāv ubhau devāvivāśvinau
en: Then, Rāma, bow in hand, having observed those two heroes who resembled each other, both like the two divine Aśvinikumāras...

translit: yannāvagacchat sugrīvaṃ vālinaṃ vāpi rāghavaḥ, tato na kṛtavānbuddhiṃ moktumantakaraṃ śaram
en: Because Rama (rāghavaḥ) did not recognize Sugriva or even Vali, he therefore did not resolve to release the death-dealing arrow.

translit: etasminnantare bhagnaḥ sugrīvastena vālinā, apaśyan rāghavaṃ nāthamṛśyamūkaṃ pradudruve
en: At that moment, Sugriva, defeated by Vali, not seeing Rama (rāghavaḥ) as his protector, fled to Mount Rishyamuka.

translit: taṃ samīkṣyāgataṃ rāmaṃ sugrīvaḥ sahalakṣmaṇam, hrīmāndīnamuvācedaṃ vasudhāmavalokayan
en: Sugrīva, having seen Rāma arrive with Lakṣmaṇa, looked down at the earth and, feeling ashamed and dejected, spoke this.

devanagari: वैरिणा घातयित्वा च किमिदानीं त्वया कृतम् ॥
translit: āhvayasveti māmuktvā darśayitvā ca vikramam, vairiṇā ghātayitvā ca kimidānīṃ tvayā kṛtam
en: After saying to me, 'Summon me!' and showing your prowess, and then having me slain by my enemy, what exactly have you done now?

devanagari: तामेव वेलां वक्तव्यं त्वया राघव तत्त्वतः ।
वालिनं न निहन्मीति ततो नाहमितो व्रजे ॥
translit: tāmeva velāṃ vaktavyaṃ tvayā rāghava tattvataḥ, vālinaṃ na nihanmīti tato nāhamito vraje
en: O Rāghava (Rāma), at that very time, you should have truly said, 'I will not kill Vāli'; then I (Sugrīva) would not have gone from here.

devanagari: त्वं च सुग्रीव वाली च सदृशौ स्थः परस्परम् ॥
translit: alaṃkāreṇa veṣeṇa pramāṇena gatena ca, tvaṃ ca sugrīva vālī ca sadṛśau sthaḥ parasparam
en: By ornamentation, by attire, by stature, and by gait, you, Sugriva, and Vali are similar to each other.

devanagari: स्वरेण वर्चसा चैव प्रेक्षितेन च वानर ।
विक्रमेण च वाक्यैश्च व्यक्तिं वां नोपलक्षये ॥
translit: svareṇa varcasā caiva prekṣitena ca vānara, vikrameṇa ca vākyaiśca vyaktiṃ vāṃ nopalakṣaye
en: O Vanara (Sugriva), I perceive no distinction between the two of you, neither by voice, nor by radiance, nor by gaze, nor by prowess, nor by words.

translit: tato'haṃ rūpasādṛśyānmohito vānarottama, notsṛjāmi mahāvegaṃ śaraṃ śatrunibarhaṇam
en: O best of monkeys, therefore, bewildered by the resemblance in appearance, I did not release the extremely swift, enemy-destroying arrow.

translit: abhijñānaṃ kuruṣva tvamātmano vānareśvara, yena tvāmabhijānīyāṃ dvandvayuddhamupāgatam
en: O lord of monkeys, create a distinguishing mark for yourself, so that I may recognize you when you enter into a duel.

devanagari: कुरु लक्ष्मण कण्ठे ऽस्य सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः ॥
translit: gajapuṣpīmimāṃ phullāmutpāṭya śubhalakṣaṇām, kuru lakṣmaṇa kaṇṭhe'sya sugrīvasya mahātmanaḥ
en: O Lakṣmaṇa, uproot this auspiciously marked, blooming Gajapuṣpī plant, and place it around the neck of this noble Sugrīva.

devanagari: लक्ष्मणो गजपुष्पीं तां तस्य कण्ठे व्यसर्जयत् ॥
translit: tato giritaṭe jātāmutpāṭya kusumāyutām, lakṣmaṇo gajapuṣpīṃ tāṃ tasya kaṇṭhe vyasarjayat
en: Then, Lakṣmaṇa uprooted that Gajapuṣpī creeper, which had grown on the mountain slope and was adorned with flowers, and placed it around Sugrīva's neck.

devanagari: स तथा शुशुभे श्रीमांल् लतया कण्ठसक्तया ।
translit: sa tathā śuśubhe śrīmāṃl latayā kaṇṭhasaktayā, mālayeva balākānāṃ sasaṃdhya iva toyadaḥ
en: Glorious, he shone with that creeper clinging to his neck, resembling a garland of cranes or a cloud illuminated by twilight.

devanagari: सर्वे ते त्वरितं गत्वा किष्किन्धां वालिपालिताम् ।
translit: sarve te tvaritaṃ gatvā kiṣkindhāṃ vālipālitām, vṛkṣairātmānamāvṛtya vyatiṣṭhan gahane vane
en: All of them, having quickly gone to Kishkindha, which was protected by Vali, concealed themselves among the trees and remained in the dense forest.

devanagari: ततः स निनदं घोरं कृत्वा युद्धाय चाह्वयत् ।
translit: tataḥ sa ninadaṃ ghoraṃ kṛtvā yuddhāya cāhvayat, parivāraiḥ parivṛto nādairbhindannivāmbaram
en: Then, surrounded by his retinue, he (Sugriva) let out a terrible roar, as if splitting the sky with his sounds, and challenged (Vali) to battle.

devanagari: अनृतं नोक्तपूर्वं मे वीर कृच्छ्रे ऽपि तिष्ठता ।
धर्मलोभपरीतेन न च वक्ष्ये कथं चन ॥
translit: anṛtaṃ noktapūrvaṃ me vīra kṛcchre'pi tiṣṭhatā, dharmalobhaparītena na ca vakṣye kathaṃ cana
en: O hero, I have never spoken an untruth, not even when I was in distress. Nor will I ever speak one, being overcome by greed for material gain (dharma).

devanagari: सुग्रीव कुरु तं शब्दं निष्पतेद् येन वानरः ॥
translit: tadāhvānanimittaṃ tvaṃ vālino hemamālinaḥ, sugrīva kuru taṃ śabdaṃ niṣpated yena vānaraḥ
en: Sugriva, in order to challenge Vali, the one adorned with a golden garland, utter that sound by which that monkey will rush out.

translit: taṃ tu tārā pariṣvajya snehāddarśitasauhṛdā, uvāca trastasaṃbhrāntā hitodarkamidaṃ vacaḥ
en: But Tara, embracing him with affection and having shown her friendliness, terrified and bewildered, spoke these words which would lead to a beneficial outcome.

translit: sādhu krodhamimaṃ vīra nadī vegamivāgatam, śayanādutthitaḥ kālyaṃ tyaja bhuktāmiva srajam
en: O hero, please abandon this anger, which has come upon you like a river's current. Having risen in the morning, cast it off as one discards a worn-out garland.

devanagari: निष्पत्य च निरस्तस्ते हन्यमानो दिशो गतः ॥
translit: pūrvamāpatitaḥ krodhāt sa tvāmāhvayate yudhi, niṣpatya ca nirastaste hanyamāno diśo gataḥ
en: Previously, having attacked you in anger, he challenges you in battle. But after rushing out, he was repelled by you, and being struck, he fled in all directions.

translit: tvayā tasya nirastasya pīḍitasya viśeṣataḥ, ihaitya punarāhvānaṃ śaṅkāṃ janayatīva me
en: His renewed challenge, particularly after he was rejected and tormented by you, and his very return here, truly causes apprehension in me.

translit: nāsahāyamahaṃ manye sugrīvaṃ tamihāgatam, avaṣṭabdhasahāyaśca yamāśrityaiṣa garjati
en: I do not believe that Sugrīva has come here without support. The one upon whom he relies, and due to whom he roars, is indeed a firm ally.

translit: prakṛtyā nipuṇaścaiva buddhimāṃścaiva vānaraḥ, aparīkṣitavīryeṇa sugrīvaḥ saha naiṣyati
en: Sugrīva, being a monkey (vānara), is by nature skillful and indeed intelligent. He would certainly not ally himself with someone whose strength has not been proven.

devanagari: पूर्वमेव मया वीर श्रुतं कथयतो वचः ।
अङ्गदस्य कुमारस्य वक्ष्यामि त्वा हितं वचः ॥
translit: pūrvameva mayā vīra śrutaṃ kathayato vacaḥ, aṅgadasya kumārasya vakṣyāmi tvā hitaṃ vacaḥ
en: O hero, I have indeed heard the words spoken by Prince Angada earlier. (But now) I will speak beneficial words to you.

translit: tava bhrāturhi vikhyātaḥ sahāyo raṇakarkaśaḥ, rāmaḥ parabalāmardī yugāntāgnirivotthitaḥ
en: Indeed, your brother's well-known ally, Rama, who is formidable in battle and the destroyer of enemy forces, has arisen like the fire at the end of a cosmic age.

translit: nivāsavṛkṣaḥ sādhūnāmāpannānāṃ parā gatiḥ, ārtānāṃ saṃśrayaścaiva yaśasaścaikabhājanam
en: He is a shelter-tree for the virtuous, the ultimate refuge for those in distress, indeed a protector for the afflicted, and the sole vessel of glory.

devanagari: तत्क्षमं न विरोधस्ते सह तेन महात्मना ।
translit: tatkṣamaṃ na virodhaste saha tena mahātmanā, durjayenāprameyena rāmeṇa raṇakarmasu
en: Therefore, it is not appropriate for you to have a conflict with that great-souled (mahātman), unconquerable, and incomparable Rama in battles.

devanagari: विग्रहं मा कृथा वीर भ्रात्रा राजन्बलीयसा ॥
translit: yauvarājyena sugrīvaṃ tūrṇaṃ sādhvabhiṣecaya, vigrahaṃ mā kṛthā vīra bhrātrā rājanbalīyasā
en: O king (rājan), quickly and properly consecrate Sugriva as the crown prince. O hero, do not engage in conflict with your more powerful brother.

devanagari: अहं हि ते क्षमं मन्ये तव रामेण सौहृदम् ।
translit: ahaṃ hi te kṣamaṃ manye tava rāmeṇa sauhṛdam, sugrīveṇa ca saṃprītiṃ vairamutsṛjya dūrataḥ
en: Indeed, I believe that friendship with Rama and good will towards Sugriva are beneficial for you, having completely abandoned hostility (vaira) far away.

devanagari: लालनीयो हि ते भ्राता यवीयानेष वानरः ।
तत्र वा सन्निहस्थो वा सर्वथा बन्धुरेव ते ॥
translit: lālanīyo hi te bhrātā yavīyāneṣa vānaraḥ, tatra vā sannihastho vā sarvathā bandhureva te
en: This younger monkey is indeed your brother and should be cherished. Whether he is there or stays here, he is always your kinsman.

devanagari: न च कार्यो विषादस्ते राघवं प्रति मत्कृते ।
translit: na ca kāryo viṣādaste rāghavaṃ prati matkṛte, dharmajñaśca kṛtajñaśca kathaṃ pāpaṃ kariṣyati
en: And you should not be grieved (viṣāda) on my account concerning Rāghava (Rāma). How could he, who understands natural law (dharma) and is grateful, commit a wrongful act?

devanagari: निवर्तस्व सह स्त्रीभिः कथं भूयो ऽनुगच्छसि ।
सौहृदं दर्शितं तारे मयि भक्तिः कृता त्वया ॥
translit: nivartasva saha strībhiḥ kathaṃ bhūyo'nugacchasi, sauhṛdaṃ darśitaṃ tāre mayi bhaktiḥ kṛtā tvayā
en: Go back with the women. Why do you continue to follow? O Tārā, you have shown your friendship and offered me your devotion (bhakti).

devanagari: दर्पं चास्य विनेष्यामि न च प्राणैर्विमोक्ष्यते ॥
translit: pratiyotsyāmyahaṃ gatvā sugrīvaṃ jahi saṃbhramam, darpaṃ cāsya vineṣyāmi na ca prāṇairvimokṣyate
en: I will go and fight back against Sugrīva. Dispel your fear. I will also destroy his pride, and he will not escape with his life.

devanagari: अहं जित्वा निवर्तिष्ये तमलं भ्रातरं रणे ॥
translit: śāpitāsi mama prāṇairnivartasva jayena ca, ahaṃ jitvā nivartiṣye tamalaṃ bhrātaraṃ raṇe
en: You are sworn by my life; turn back, assured of victory. I will conquer that formidable brother of mine in battle and then return.

devanagari: तं तु तारा परिष्वज्य वालिनं प्रियवादिनी ।
चकार रुदती मन्दं दक्षिणा सा प्रदक्षिणम् ॥
translit: taṃ tu tārā pariṣvajya vālinaṃ priyavādinī, cakāra rudatī mandaṃ dakṣiṇā sā pradakṣiṇam
en: But that sweet-speaking Tārā, embracing Vālin, tearfully and slowly performed circumambulation (pradakṣiṇam) to his right side.

translit: tataḥ svastyayanaṃ kṛtvā mantravadvijayaiṣiṇī, antaḥpuraṃ saha strībhiḥ praviṣṭā śokamohitā
en: Then, after performing a ritual for well-being (svastyayana) with appropriate mantras, she, seeking victory (for Vali) and overcome by sorrow, entered the inner palace (antaḥpura) with the other women.

translit: tato dhanuṣi saṃdhāya śaramāśīviṣopamam, rāghaveṇa mahābāṇo vālivakṣasi pātitaḥ
en: Then, after affixing an arrow resembling a venomous serpent to the bow, a mighty arrow was shot by Rama (rāghaveṇa) into Vali's chest.

translit: athokṣitaḥ śoṇitatoyavisravaiḥ supuṣpitāśoka ivāniloddhataḥ, vicetano vāsavasūnurāhave prabhraṃśitendradhvajavat kṣitiṃ gataḥ
en: Then, the son of Indra (Vāsava), rendered unconscious in battle, fell to the ground. He was drenched by streams of blood-water, resembling a beautiful Ashoka tree in full bloom that has been uprooted by the wind, and was like Indra's fallen banner.

devanagari: पपात सहसा वाली निकृत्त इव पादपः ॥
translit: tataḥ śareṇābhihato rāmeṇa raṇakarkaśaḥ, papāta sahasā vālī nikṛtta iva pādapaḥ
en: Then, Vali, who was fierce in battle, was struck by an arrow from Rama, and suddenly fell like a cut-down tree.

devanagari: न श्रीर्जहाति न प्राणा न तेजो न पराक्रमः ॥
translit: bhūmau nipatitasyāpi tasya dehaṃ mahātmanaḥ, na śrīrjahāti na prāṇā na tejo na parākramaḥ
en: Even though the body of that great soul (mahātman) had fallen to the ground, neither his splendor (śrī), his life-breath (prāṇa), his vigor, nor his prowess abandoned him.

devanagari: दधार हरिमुख्यस्य प्राणांस्तेजः श्रियं च सा ॥
translit: śakradattā varā mālā kāñcanī ratnabhūṣitā, dadhāra harimukhyasya prāṇāṃstejaḥ śriyaṃ ca sā
en: The excellent golden garland, adorned with jewels, which was given by Indra (Śakra), sustained the life-breath (prāṇa), vigor, and splendor (śrī) of the chief of the monkeys.

devanagari: तस्य माला च देहश्च मर्मघाती च यः शरः ।
translit: tasya mālā ca dehaśca marmaghātī ca yaḥ śaraḥ, tridheva racitā lakṣmīḥ patitasyāpi śobhate
en: His garland, his body, and the deadly arrow that struck his vital points - these three, as if a single splendor (lakṣmī) arranged in three parts, shone beautifully, even for him who had fallen.

devanagari: पराङ्मुखवधं कृत्वा को नु प्राप्तस्त्वया गुणः ।
translit: parāṅmukhavadhaṃ kṛtvā ko nu prāptastvayā guṇaḥ, yadahaṃ yuddhasaṃrabdhastvatkṛte nidhanaṃ gataḥ
en: What merit have you gained by slaying one who had turned his back? Because of you, I, eager for battle, have met my demise.

devanagari: रामः करुणवेदी च प्रजानां च हिते रतः ॥
translit: kulīnaḥ sattvasaṃpannastejasvī caritavrataḥ, rāmaḥ karuṇavedī ca prajānāṃ ca hite rataḥ
en: Rāma is of noble lineage, endowed with strength and courage, radiant with spiritual power, and one who observes his vows. He is also acquainted with compassion and devoted to the welfare of his subjects.

devanagari: इति ते सर्वभूतानि कथयन्ति यशो भुवि ॥
translit: sānukrośo mahotsāhaḥ samayajño dṛḍhavrataḥ, iti te sarvabhūtāni kathayanti yaśo bhuvi
en: Compassionate, greatly enthusiastic, knowing what is proper, and firm in his vows – thus all beings on earth speak of your fame.

translit: tān guṇān saṃpradhāryāhamagryaṃ cābhijanaṃ tava, tārayā pratiṣiddhaḥ san sugrīveṇa samāgataḥ
en: Having thoroughly considered those qualities and your noble lineage, I then, despite being forbidden by Tara, joined with Sugriva.

translit: na māmanyena saṃrabdhaṃ pramattaṃ veddhumarhasi, iti me buddhirutpannā babhūvādarśane tava
en: You should not strike me, who is provoked by another and unaware. This was the thought that arose in my mind when you were not visible.

translit: na tvāṃ vinihatātmānaṃ dharmadhvajamadhārmikam, jāne pāpasamācāraṃ tṛṇaiḥ kūpamivāvṛtam
en: I did not recognize you as one whose inner self (ātman) is ruined, a hypocritical banner of (dharma) righteousness, whose conduct is sinful, like a well covered by grass.

devanagari: विषये वा पुरे वा ते यदा नापकरोम्यहम् ।
न च त्वां प्रतिजाने ऽहं कस्मात्त्वं हंस्यकिल्बिषम् ॥
translit: viṣaye vā pure vā te yadā nāpakaromyaham, na ca tvāṃ pratijāne'haṃ kasmāttvaṃ haṃsyakilbiṣam
en: When I do no harm to your territory or city, nor do I challenge you, why do you kill me, an innocent one?

translit: phalamūlāśanaṃ nityaṃ vānaraṃ vanagocaram, māmihāpratiyudhyantamanyena ca samāgatam
en: Why do you kill me, a monkey, who habitually consumes fruits and roots, who roams the forest, who is not fighting back here, and who is already engaged with another (foe)?

translit: vayaṃ vanacarā rāma mṛgā mūlaphalāśanāḥ, eṣā prakṛtirasmākaṃ puruṣastvaṃ nareśvaraḥ
en: O Rama, we are forest-dwellers, animals (mṛga), whose food is roots and fruits. This is our intrinsic nature (prakṛti), while you are a king, the lord of men (puruṣa).

devanagari: भूमिर्हिरण्यं रूप्यं च निग्रहे कारणानि च ।
तत्र कस्ते वने लोभो मदीयेषु फलेषु वा ॥
translit: bhūmirhiraṇyaṃ rūpyaṃ ca nigrahe kāraṇāni ca, tatra kaste vane lobho madīyeṣu phaleṣu vā
en: Land, gold, and silver are typically the reasons for subjugation. Therefore, what is your avarice in the forest, or for fruits belonging to me?

devanagari: अद्य वैवस्वतं देवं पश्येस्त्वं निहतो मया ॥
translit: dṛśyamānastu yudhyethā mayā yudhi nṛpātmaja, adya vaivasvataṃ devaṃ paśyestvaṃ nihato mayā
en: O prince, if you were to fight me openly in battle, revealing yourself, then today you would be struck down by me and encounter Yama, the god of death.

devanagari: त्वयादृश्येन तु रणे निहतो ऽहं दुरासदः ।
translit: tvayādṛśyena tu raṇe nihato'haṃ durāsadaḥ, prasuptaḥ pannageneva naraḥ pānavaśaṃ gataḥ
en: Indeed, I, who am unassailable, have been slain by you, who were unseen in battle. It is like a man fallen under the sway of intoxication (pānavasaṃ), when asleep, being bitten by a snake.

devanagari: कण्ठे बद्ध्वा प्रदद्यां ते ऽनिहतं रावणं रणे ॥
translit: sugrīvapriyakāmena yadahaṃ nihatastvayā, kaṇṭhe baddhvā pradadyāṃ te'nihataṃ rāvaṇaṃ raṇe
en: Because I was slain by you, out of your desire for Sugrīva's welfare, I would have seized the unslain Rāvaṇa by the neck and handed him over to you in battle.

devanagari: न्यस्तां सागरतोये वा पाताले वापि मैथिलीम् ।
translit: nyastāṃ sāgaratoye vā pātāle vāpi maithilīm, jānayeyaṃ tavādeśācchvetāmaśvatarīmiva
en: By your command, I would ascertain the whereabouts of Maithilī (Sītā), even if she were placed in the ocean's waters or indeed in the netherworld (pātāla), just as one would recognize a white she-mule.

devanagari: युक्तं यत् प्रप्नुयाद् राज्यं सुग्रीवः स्वर्गते मयि ।
translit: yuktaṃ yat prapnuyād rājyaṃ sugrīvaḥ svargate mayi, ayuktaṃ yadadharmeṇa tvayāhaṃ nihato raṇe
en: It is proper that Sugrīva should obtain the kingdom upon my departure to heaven. However, it is improper that I was slain by you in battle through an act contrary to natural law (adharma).

translit: ikṣvākūṇāmiyaṃ bhūmiḥ saśailavanakānanā, mṛgapakṣimanuṣyāṇāṃ nigrahānugrahāvapi
en: This land, with its mountains, forests, and groves, belongs to the Ikshvakus, and they also have the power to punish and protect (or control and favor) animals, birds, and humans.

translit: tāṃ pālayati dharmātmā bharataḥ satyavāgṛjuḥ, dharmakāmārthatattvajño nigrahānugrahe rataḥ
en: Bharata, whose intrinsic nature (dharma) is righteousness, and who is truthful and straightforward, governs the land. He understands the essence of natural law (dharma), desire, and prosperity, and judiciously applies both punishment and favor.

translit: tasya dharmakṛtādeśā vayamanye ca pārthivaḥ, carāmo vasudhāṃ kṛtsnāṃ dharmasaṃtānamicchavaḥ
en: We, along with other rulers, act by his (Bharata's) directives which are founded upon natural law (dharma). We traverse the entire earth, seeking the perpetuation of natural law (dharma).

devanagari: ज्येष्ठो भ्राता पिता चैव यश्च विद्यां प्रयच्छति ।
त्रयस्ते पितरो ज्ञेया धर्मे च पथि वर्तिनः ॥
translit: jyeṣṭho bhrātā pitā caiva yaśca vidyāṃ prayacchati, trayaste pitaro jñeyā dharme ca pathi vartinaḥ
en: The elder brother, the father, and he who imparts knowledge - these three are to be understood as fathers, particularly if they are steadfast on the path of righteousness (dharma).

translit: yavīyānātmanaḥ putraḥ śiṣyaścāpi guṇoditaḥ, putravatte trayaścintyā dharmaścedatra kāraṇam
en: The younger brother, one's own son, and a disciple endowed with good qualities - these three should be regarded as equivalent to a son, if adherence to natural law (dharma) is the guiding principle in this matter.

translit: sūkṣmaḥ paramadurjñeyaḥ satāṃ dharmaḥ plavaṃgama, hṛdisthaḥ sarvabhūtānāmātmā veda śubhāśubham
en: O monkey, the intrinsic nature (dharma) of the virtuous is subtle and exceedingly difficult to comprehend. The self (ātman), residing within the heart of all beings, knows what is auspicious and inauspicious.

devanagari: तदेतत् कारणं पश्य यदर्थं त्वं मया हतः ।
translit: tadetat kāraṇaṃ paśya yadarthaṃ tvaṃ mayā hataḥ, bhrāturvartasi bhāryāyāṃ tyaktvā dharmaṃ sanātanam
en: Behold this reason for which you were slain by me: you have abandoned the eternal natural law (dharma) and are engaging with your brother's wife.

translit: asya tvaṃ dharamāṇasya sugrīvasya mahātmanaḥ, rumāyāṃ vartase kāmāt snuṣāyāṃ pāpakarmakṛt
en: O perpetrator of sinful deeds! You dwell with Rumā, the wife of the great-souled Sugriva, who is still alive, driven by lust, (treating her as if she were your own) daughter-in-law.

translit: tadvyatītasya te dharmāt kāmavṛttasya vānara, bhrātṛbhāryābhimarśe'smindaṇḍo'yaṃ pratipāditaḥ
en: Therefore, O monkey, this punishment has been meted out to you, who have transgressed the natural law (dharma) and whose conduct is driven by desire, for this offense of violating a brother's wife.

devanagari: औरसीं भगिनीं वापि भार्यां वाप्यनुजस्य यः ।
प्रचरेत नरः कामात्तस्य दण्डो वधः स्मृतः ॥
translit: aurasīṃ bhaginīṃ vāpi bhāryāṃ vāpyanujasya yaḥ, pracareta naraḥ kāmāttasya daṇḍo vadhaḥ smṛtaḥ
en: The man who, driven by lust, violates his own sister, or even his younger brother's wife, for him, the punishment declared is death.

devanagari: सुग्रीवेण च मे सख्यं लक्ष्मणेन यथा तथा ।
दारराज्यनिमित्तं च निःश्रेयसि रतः स मे ॥
translit: sugrīveṇa ca me sakhyaṃ lakṣmaṇena yathā tathā, dārarājyanimittaṃ ca niḥśreyasi rataḥ sa me
en: My friendship with Sugrīva is indeed just like my friendship with Lakṣmaṇa. And he (Sugrīva), for the sake of his wife and kingdom, is devoted to my supreme welfare.

devanagari: प्रतिज्ञा च मया दत्ता तदा वानरसंनिधौ ।
translit: pratijñā ca mayā dattā tadā vānarasaṃnidhau, pratijñā ca kathaṃ śakyā madvidhenānavekṣitum
en: A vow was given by me then, in the presence of the monkeys. And how can a vow be disregarded by someone like me?
Men, with various nets, nooses, and traps, both hidden and visible, catch very many animals (mṛga) – whether they are fleeing, or terrified, or confident and very settled in their place.

devanagari: विध्यन्ति विमुखांश्चापि न च दोषो ऽत्र विद्यते ॥
translit: pramattānapramattān vā narā māṃsārthino bhṛśam, vidhyanti vimukhāṃścāpi na ca doṣo'tra vidyate
en: People who are intensely desirous of meat kill animals, whether they are heedless or attentive, and even those that are fleeing or have turned away; and there is no fault in this action.

devanagari: तस्मात्त्वं निहतो युद्धे मया बाणेन वानर ।
en: Here, royal sages who are knowledgeable in natural law (dharma) go hunting. Therefore, O monkey, you have been struck down in battle by my arrow, because you are a tree-dwelling animal (śākhāmṛga), whether you were fighting or not fighting.

translit: evamuktastu rāmeṇa vālī pravyathito bhṛśam, pratyuvāca tato rāmaṃ prāñjalirvānareśvaraḥ
en: Vali, thus addressed by Rama, became greatly distressed. Then the lord of monkeys, with folded hands, replied to Rama.

translit: yattvamāttha naraśreṣṭha tadevaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ, prativaktuṃ prakṛṣṭe hi nāpakṛṣṭastu śaknuyāt
en: O best among men, what you say is indeed so; there is no doubt about it. For an inferior person truly cannot reply to a superior one.

devanagari: न त्वात्मानमहं शोचे न तारां नापि बान्धवान् ।
translit: na tvātmānamahaṃ śoce na tārāṃ nāpi bāndhavān, yathā putraṃ guṇaśreṣṭhamaṅgadaṃ kanakāṅgadam
en: I do not grieve for myself (ātman), nor for Tara, nor for my relatives, as much as I grieve for my son Angada, who is excellent in qualities and wears golden armlets.

translit: sa mamādarśanāddīno bālyāt prabhṛti lālitaḥ, taṭāka iva pītāmburupaśoṣaṃ gamiṣyati
en: He, who has been cherished by me since childhood, will become dejected due to my absence and will waste away like a pond whose water has been drunk.

devanagari: त्वं हि शास्ता च गोप्ता च कार्याकार्यविधौ स्थितः ॥
translit: sugrīve cāṅgade caiva vidhatsva matimuttamām, tvaṃ hi śāstā ca goptā ca kāryākāryavidhau sthitaḥ
en: You should extend your best counsel to Sugriva and Angada. For you are indeed the instructor and protector, well-versed in determining what is proper action (kārya) and what is improper (akārya).

devanagari: या ते नरपते वृत्तिर्भरते लक्ष्मणे च या ।
translit: yā te narapate vṛttirbharate lakṣmaṇe ca yā, sugrīve cāṅgade rājaṃstāṃ cintayitumarhasi
en: O king, you should show the same consideration (vṛtti) towards Sugriva and Angada as you do towards Bharata and Lakshmana.

translit: maddoṣakṛtadoṣāṃ tāṃ yathā tārāṃ tapasvinīm, sugrīvo nāvamanyeta tathāvasthātumarhasi
en: You should act in such a way that Sugriva does not disrespect the distressed Tara, whose misfortune was caused by my fault.

devanagari: गतः स्वां प्रकृतिं धर्म्यां धर्मदृष्ट्तेन वर्त्मना ॥
translit: tadbhavāndaṇḍasaṃyogādasmādvigatakalmaṣaḥ, gataḥ svāṃ prakṛtiṃ dharmyāṃ dharmadṛṣṭtena vartmanā
en: Therefore, you, through the contact with this staff (daṇḍa), are now freed from all impurities. You have regained your intrinsic nature (prakṛti), which is aligned with righteousness (dharma), by following a path illuminated by natural law (dharma).

devanagari: पुत्रेण मम किं कार्यं किं राज्येन किमात्मना ।
translit: putreṇa mama kiṃ kāryaṃ kiṃ rājyena kimātmanā, kapisiṃhe mahābhāge tasminbhartari naśyati
en: What is the use of a son to me? What is the use of a kingdom? What is the use of my very self (ātman), now that my greatly blessed husband, that lion among monkeys, is perishing?

translit: pādamūlaṃ gamiṣyāmi tasyaivāhaṃ mahātmanaḥ, yo'sau rāmaprayuktena śareṇa vinipātitaḥ
en: I will go to the very feet of that great-souled (mahātman) one, who was struck down by an arrow dispatched by Rāma.

translit: evamuktvā pradudrāva rudatī śokakarśitā, śiraścoraśca bāhubhyāṃ duḥkhena samabhighnatī
en: Having spoken thus, emaciated by sorrow, she ran forward weeping, sorrowfully striking her head and chest with both her arms.

devanagari: सुग्रीवस्य त्वया भार्या हृता स च विवासितः ।
translit: sugrīvasya tvayā bhāryā hṛtā sa ca vivāsitaḥ, yattattasya tvayā vyuṣṭiḥ prāpteyaṃ plavagādhipa
en: By you, Sugriva's wife was taken and he was exiled. O king of monkeys (plavagādhipa), for that act, this consequence (vyuṣṭi) has now befallen you.

translit: niḥśreyasaparā mohāttvayā cāhaṃ vigarhitā, yaiṣābruvaṃ hitaṃ vākyaṃ vānarendrahitaiṣiṇī
en: And I, who was devoted to the highest good and was a well-wisher for the king of monkeys, was scorned by you out of delusion when I spoke this beneficial word.

translit: lālitaścāṅgado vīraḥ sukumāraḥ sukhocitaḥ, vatsyate kāmavasthāṃ me pitṛvye krodhamūrchite
en: And the valiant Aṅgada, who is cherished, tender, and accustomed to comfort - in what condition will he, for my sake, live with his uncle (Sugrīva) who is overwhelmed by rage?

devanagari: दुर्लभं दर्शनं त्वस्य तव वत्स भविष्यति ॥
translit: kuruṣva pitaraṃ putra sudṛṣṭaṃ dharmavatsalam, durlabhaṃ darśanaṃ tvasya tava vatsa bhaviṣyati
en: O son, gaze well upon your father, who is affectionate towards the constitution (dharma); for indeed, his sight will become rare for you, my child.

devanagari: रामेण हि महत् कर्म कृतं त्वामभिनिघ्नता ।
आनृण्यं तु गतं तस्य सुग्रीवस्य प्रतिश्रवे ॥
translit: rāmeṇa hi mahat karma kṛtaṃ tvāmabhinighnatā, ānṛṇyaṃ tu gataṃ tasya sugrīvasya pratiśrave
en: Indeed, a great act was performed by Rama by striking you down. But his (Rama's) obligation (ānṛṇyam), made in accordance with Sugriva's vow, has now been fulfilled.

devanagari: किमप्रियं ते प्रियचारुवेष कृतं मया नाथ सुतेन वा ते ।
सहायिनीमद्य विहाय वीर यमक्षयं गच्छसि दुर्विनीतम् ॥
translit: kimapriyaṃ te priyacāruveṣa kṛtaṃ mayā nātha sutena vā te, sahāyinīmadya vihāya vīra yamakṣayaṃ gacchasi durvinītam
en: O lord, O dear one of charming form, what wrong has been done to you by me or by your son? O hero, you imprudent one, abandoning your companion today, you go to the abode of Yama (yamakṣaya)?

devanagari: यद्यप्रियं किं चिदसंप्रधार्य कृतं मया स्यात्तव दीर्घबाहो ।
क्षमस्व मे तद्धरिवंश नाथ व्रजामि मूर्ध्ना तव वीर पादौ ॥
translit: yadyapriyaṃ kiṃ cidasaṃpradhārya kṛtaṃ mayā syāttava dīrghabāho, kṣamasva me taddharivaṃśa nātha vrajāmi mūrdhnā tava vīra pādau
en: If by me, without consideration, something disagreeable has been done to you, O long-armed one, then forgive me for that, O lord of the monkey lineage. O hero, I prostrate myself at your feet with my head.

translit: sugrīvadoṣeṇa na māṃ gantumarhasi kilbiṣāt, kṛṣyamāṇaṃ bhaviṣyeṇa buddhimohena māṃ balāt
en: You should not incur any wrongdoing (kilbiṣa) concerning me due to Sugriva's fault, for I am being forcibly dragged away by destiny and by a delusion of intellect.

translit: yugapadvihitaṃ tāta na manye sukhamāvayoḥ, sauhārdaṃ bhrātṛyuktaṃ hi tadidaṃ jātamanyathā
en: Dear one, I do not believe that happiness for us both was simultaneously ordained. Indeed, this brotherly affection has turned out quite differently.

translit: pratipadya tvamadyaiva rājyameṣāṃ vanaukasām, māmapyadyaiva gacchantaṃ viddhi vaivasvatakṣayam
en: You, right now, accept the kingship over these forest dwellers. And know that I too am departing right now to the abode of Yama (death).

translit: sukhārhaṃ sukhasaṃvṛddhaṃ bālamenamabāliśam, bāṣpapūrṇamukhaṃ paśya bhūmau patitamaṅgadam
en: Behold this Angada, a child who deserves comfort and was raised in comfort, yet is not foolish. See him with a face full of tears, fallen on the ground.

translit: mama prāṇaiḥ priyataraṃ putraṃ putramivaurasaṃ, mayā hīnamahīnārthaṃ sarvataḥ paripālaya
en: (tvam) mama prāṇaiḥ priyataram putram aurasam putram

devanagari: त्वमप्यस्य हि दाता च परित्राता च सर्वतः ।
translit: tvamapyasya hi dātā ca paritrātā ca sarvataḥ, bhayeṣvabhayadaścaiva yathāhaṃ plavageśvara
en: O lord of monkeys, you, indeed, are his provider and his complete protector from all quarters. You are also the one who gives him fearlessness in times of danger, just as I was.

translit: suṣeṇaduhitā ceyamarthasūkṣmaviniścaye, autpātike ca vividhe sarvataḥ pariniṣṭhitā
en: And this daughter of Suṣeṇa is fully proficient in discerning subtle meanings and in various kinds of portents.

devanagari: न हि तारामतं किं चिदन्यथा परिवर्तते ॥
translit: yadeṣā sādhviti brūyāt kāryaṃ tanmuktasaṃśayam, na hi tārāmataṃ kiṃ cidanyathā parivartate
en: Whatever she declares to be correct, that course of action is undoubtedly sound. Indeed, Tārā's opinion never proves to be wrong.

translit: rāghavasya ca te kāryaṃ kartavyamaviśaṅkayā, syādadharmo hyakaraṇe tvāṃ ca hiṃsyādvimānitaḥ
en: And you must perform Rāghava's (Rāma's) task without hesitation. Indeed, non-performance would constitute a violation of natural law (dharma), and a dishonored Rāma might harm you.

devanagari: उदारा श्रीः स्थिता ह्यस्यां संप्रजह्यान्मृते मयि ॥
translit: imāṃ ca mālāmādhatsva divyāṃ sugrīvakāñcanīm, udārā śrīḥ sthitā hyasyāṃ saṃprajahyānmṛte mayi
en: And, O Sugriva, wear this divine, golden garland. Indeed, exalted fortune (śrī) resides in it, but this (fortune) would completely abandon it upon my death.

translit: ityevamuktaḥ sugrīvo vālinā bhrātṛsauhṛdāt, harṣaṃ tyaktvā punardīno grahagrasta ivoḍurāṭ
en: Thus spoken to by Vālī out of brotherly affection, Sugriva, having abandoned his joy, again became dejected, like the moon (uḍurāṭ) seized by an eclipse.

devanagari: जग्राह सो ऽभ्यनुज्ञातो मालां तां चैव काञ्चनीम् ॥
translit: tadvālivacanācchāntaḥ kurvanyuktamatandritaḥ, jagrāha so'bhyanujñāto mālāṃ tāṃ caiva kāñcanīm
en: Calmed by Vālī's words, and acting properly and vigilantly, he (Sugriva), having been permitted, indeed took that golden garland.

translit: deśakālau bhajasvādya kṣamamāṇaḥ priyāpriye, sukhaduḥkhasahaḥ kāle sugrīvavaśago bhava
en: Today, you should adapt yourself to the specific time and circumstances, patiently enduring both favorable and unfavorable experiences. Tolerant of happiness and sorrow, be obedient to Sugrīva when the time is right.

translit: māsyāmitrairgataṃ gacchermā śatrubhirariṃdama, bharturarthaparo dāntaḥ sugrīvavaśago bhava
en: O destroyer of foes, do not associate with his enemies, nor with any other adversaries. You must be dedicated to your master's purpose, be self-controlled, and remain subservient to Sugrīva.

devanagari: न चातिप्रणयः कार्यः कर्तव्यो ऽप्रणयश्च ते ।
translit: na cātipraṇayaḥ kāryaḥ kartavyo'praṇayaśca te, ubhayaṃ hi mahādoṣaṃ tasmādantaradṛgbhava
en: Neither excessive familiarity should be shown by you, nor should a complete lack of familiarity be displayed. For both of these are indeed great flaws. Therefore, be discerning.

translit: ityuktvātha vivṛttākṣaḥ śarasaṃpīḍito bhṛśam, vivṛtairdaśanairbhīmairbabhūvotkrāntajīvitaḥ
en: Having spoken thus, he (Valin), with eyes wide open, deeply afflicted by the arrows, and with dreadful, exposed teeth, then expired.

devanagari: ततस्तु तारा व्यसनार्णव प्लुता मृतस्या भर्तुर्वदनं समीक्ष्य सा ।
जगाम भूमिं परिरभ्य वालिनं महाद्रुमं छिन्नमिवाश्रिता लता ॥
translit: tatastu tārā vyasanārṇava plutā mṛtasyā bharturvadanaṃ samīkṣya sā, jagāma bhūmiṃ parirabhya vālinaṃ mahādrumaṃ chinnamivāśritā latā
en: Then, Tara, submerged in an ocean of grief, beholding the face of her dead husband, fell to the ground, embracing Valin, like a creeper clinging to a great felled tree.

devanagari: अवस्थां पश्चिमां पश्य पितुः पुत्र सुदारुणाम् ।
translit: avasthāṃ paścimāṃ paśya pituḥ putra sudāruṇām, saṃprasaktasya vairasya gato'ntaḥ pāpakarmaṇā
en: Son, behold your father's dreadful final condition. The deeply ingrained enmity, brought about by sinful actions, has reached its end.

translit: bālasūryodayatanuṃ prayāntaṃ yamasādanam, abhivādaya rājānaṃ pitaraṃ putra mānadam
en: Son, salute your father, the honorable king, whose body resembles the rising sun, as he departs to the abode of Yama.

translit: evamuktaḥ samutthāya jagrāha caraṇau pituḥ, bhujābhyāṃ pīnavṛtābhyāmaṅgado'hamiti bruvan
en: Thus addressed, he rose up and grasped his father's feet with his strong, thick arms, saying, 'I am Angada'.

translit: abhivādayamānaṃ tvāmaṅgadaṃ tvaṃ yathāpurā, dīrghāyurbhava putreti kimarthaṃ nābhibhāṣase
en: Why do you not address Angada, who is saluting you, and say 'Be long-lived, O son,' as you did formerly?

devanagari: या दत्ता देवराजेन तव तुष्टेन संयुगे ।
शातकुम्भमयीं मालां तां ते पश्यामि नेह किम् ॥
translit: yā dattā devarājena tava tuṣṭena saṃyuge, śātakumbhamayīṃ mālāṃ tāṃ te paśyāmi neha kim
en: Why do I not see here that golden garland of yours which was given to you by the delighted king of gods (Indra) in battle?

translit: gatāsuṃ vālinaṃ dṛṣṭvā rāghavastadanantaram, abravīt praśritaṃ vākyaṃ sugrīvaṃ śatrutāpanaḥ
en: Seeing Vali, whose life had departed, the scorcher of enemies, Rama (Rāghava), then spoke gentle words to Sugriva.
You see this crowd, so deeply afflicted by sorrow, yet why is your face, O giver of honor, joyful even in death? It appears the color of the setting sun, as if you are still alive.

devanagari: एष त्वां रामरूपेण कालः कर्षति वानर ।
येन स्म विधवाः सर्वाः कृता एकेषुणा रणे ॥
translit: eṣa tvāṃ rāmarūpeṇa kālaḥ karṣati vānara, yena sma vidhavāḥ sarvāḥ kṛtā ekeṣuṇā raṇe
en: O Vanara, it is Death, in the guise of Rama, who drags you away, the very one by whom all these women have been made widows with a single arrow in this battle.

translit: sugrīveṇa tataḥ sārdhamaṅgadaḥ pitaraṃ rudan, citāmāropayāmāsa śokenābhihatendriyaḥ
en: Then, Angada, weeping and whose senses were overwhelmed by grief, along with Sugriva, placed his father on the funeral pyre.

devanagari: ततो ऽग्निं विधिवद्दत्त्वा सो ऽपसव्यं चकार ह ।
translit: tato'gniṃ vidhivaddattvā so'pasavyaṃ cakāra ha, pitaraṃ dīrghamadhvānaṃ prasthitaṃ vyākulendriyaḥ
en: Then, having ritually offered the fire, he (Angada), whose senses were agitated, performed the ritual anti-clockwise circumambulation for his father, who had set out on the long journey (of death).

translit: sugrīveṇaiva dīnena dīno bhūtvā mahābalaḥ, samānaśokaḥ kākutsthaḥ pretakāryāṇyakārayat
en: The mighty Kakutstha (Rama), sharing the same sorrow as the distressed Sugriva, became sorrowful himself and arranged for the performance of the funeral rites for the deceased.

devanagari: चतुर्दशसमाः सौम्य ग्रामं वा यदि वा पुरम् ।
translit: caturdaśasamāḥ saumya grāmaṃ vā yadi vā puram, na pravekṣyāmi hanumanpiturnirdeśapālakaḥ
en: O gentle Hanumān, I, as a follower of my father's command, will not enter any village or city for fourteen years.

translit: susamṛddhāṃ guhāṃ divyāṃ sugrīvo vānararṣabhaḥ, praviṣṭo vidhivadvīraḥ kṣipraṃ rājye'bhiṣicyatām
en: Let Sugrīva, the heroic chief of monkeys, having properly entered the very prosperous and splendid cave, be swiftly consecrated to the kingship.

translit: evamuktvā hanūmantaṃ rāmaḥ sugrīvamabravīt, imamapyaṅgadaṃ vīra yauvarājye'bhiṣecaya
en: Having thus spoken to Hanumān, Rāma then said to Sugrīva: 'O hero, also consecrate this Aṅgada to the position of crown prince.'

devanagari: पूर्वो ऽयं वार्षिको मासः श्रावणः सलिलागमः ।
translit: pūrvo'yaṃ vārṣiko māsaḥ śrāvaṇaḥ salilāgamaḥ, pravṛttāḥ saumya catvāro māsā vārṣikasaṃjñitāḥ
en: O gentle one, this month of Shravana, which is the first of the rainy season and marks the arrival of the waters, has now begun. The four months designated as the rainy season have commenced.

translit: nāyamudyogasamayaḥ praviśa tvaṃ purīṃ śubhām, asmin vatsyāmyahaṃ saumya parvate sahalakṣmaṇaḥ
en: This is not the time for enterprise. You, O gentle one, should enter your beautiful city. I, along with Lakshmana, will reside on this mountain.

devanagari: रामस्य तु वचः कुर्वन् सुग्रीवो हरिपुंगवः ।
translit: rāmasya tu vacaḥ kurvan sugrīvo haripuṃgavaḥ, aṅgadaṃ saṃpariṣvajya yauvarājye'bhiṣecayat
en: Sugriva, the chief of monkeys, indeed, obeying the word of Rama, first fully embraced Angada, and then consecrated him to the position of crown prince.
